title: "![](assets/logo.svg){.brand-mark .light-content}![](assets/logo-dark.svg){.brand-mark .dark-content}**laplacekit**"
---

An extensible, modern Laplace-approximation library for PyTorch, built on a plugin system.

Curvatures, likelihoods, priors, predictives and model integrations are all plugins, and even the built-in ones are written as plugins!
It runs on `torch.func` and Curvlinops.
The goal is flexibility and extensibility: every Laplace method, on any model.

```bash
pip install laplacekit
```

## First-party plugins

The first-party plugins cover Hugging Face `transformers` and `diffusers` models, reward models (Bradley–Terry likelihood), subnetwork Laplace, heteroscedastic Laplace, function-space (GP) Laplace, and marginal-likelihood training.
The [Quickstart](quickstart/basics.py) has a page for each.

To install all of them:

```bash
pip install "laplacekit[all]"
```

Or one at a time:

```bash
pip install "laplacekit[transformers]"
pip install "laplacekit[diffusers]"
pip install "laplacekit[subnet]"
pip install "laplacekit[heteroscedastic]"
pip install "laplacekit[reward]"
pip install "laplacekit[gp]"
pip install "laplacekit[marglik]"
```

## Examples

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Classifier

```diff
+ import laplacekit as lk

  model = train(model, train_loader)
  logits = model(x_test)
- probs = logits.softmax(-1)
+ post = lk.laplace(model, train_loader, likelihood=lk.Categorical())
+ probs = lk.predict(post, x_test).probs
```

### Regression

```diff
+ import laplacekit as lk

  model = train(model, train_loader)
- y_pred = model(x_test)
+ post = lk.laplace(model, train_loader, likelihood=lk.Gaussian())
+ pred = lk.predict(post, x_test)
+ y_pred, y_std = pred.mean, pred.stddev
```

### Language model

```diff
+ import laplacekit as lk

  model = train(get_peft_model(model, lora_config), train_loader)
  inputs = tokenizer(prompts, return_tensors="pt", padding=True)
- probs = model(**inputs).logits[:, -1].softmax(-1)
+ post = lk.transformers.laplace_lora(model, train_loader)
+ probs = lk.predict(post, inputs, select=lk.transformers.last_token).probs
```

:::
